## DataCite Corpus - Exploratory Analysis

We first look at the number and proportions of values in the DataCite corpus that are missing values for relevant variables: publication DOI/identifier, dataset creation date, article publication date, and funder information. We also return the total number of observations in the DataCite Corpus and the number of observations where the NIH is listed as a funder.

```{r get_dc_summary, cache = TRUE}
#### FUNCTION: get_dc_summary - argument filename (string) ####
## Argument filename takes the name of a DataCite Corpus
## file. Column names are assumed to match the columns 
## provided in the DataCite Corpus as of 11 October 2026. 
## Documentation and file downloads available 
## at https://zenodo.org/records/16901115

get_dc_summary <- function(filename) {
  ## Returns descriptive statistics of the data file - number
  ## of rows, number & proportion of rows with publication DOIs, 
  ## number & proportion of rows with a 'created' date,
  ## number & proportion of rows with publication dates,
  ## number & proportion of rows with a funder listed.
  
  dat <- read_csv(file = filename, na = c("", "NA", "none"))
  
  summarylist <- dat |> summarise(
    n = nrow(dat),
    n_doi = str_detect(dat$publication, pattern = "doi") |> sum(na.rm = TRUE),
    n_created_date = sum(1 - is.na(dat$created), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_pub_date = sum(1 - is.na(dat$publishedDate), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_funders = sum(1 - is.na(dat$funders), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_nih = str_detect(dat$funders, pattern = "(NIH)|(National Institutes of Health)") |> 
      sum(na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |> unlist()
  
  return(summarylist)
}

#### FUNCTION: summary_datacite - argument filenames (string or vector of strings) ####
## Argument filenames stores names of DataCite Corpus files. 
## Calls  get_dc_summary to compute summary statistics for 
## each data file, returns a dataset.
summary_datacite <- function(filenames) {
  cl <- makeCluster(8)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  
  summ_dc <- foreach(
    fn = filenames,
    .combine = "rbind",
    .export = "get_dc_summary",
    .packages = "tidyverse"
  ) %dopar% {
    get_dc_summary(fn)
  }
  
  stopCluster(cl)
  
  return(summ_dc)
}

#### Call summary_datacite ####

# Call summary_datacite, get dataset of summary statistics for
# each data file, reset row names to indexes
summary_dat <- summary_datacite(files) |> as.data.frame()
row.names(summary_dat) <- c(1:nrow(summary_dat))

# Compute summary statistics across summary_dat (for whole dataset)
summary_dat |> summarise(
  N.obs = sum(n),
  N.doi = sum(n_doi),
  Prop.doi = sum(n_doi) / sum(n),
  N.cr.date = sum(n_created_date),
  Prop.cr.date = sum(n_created_date) / sum(n),
  N.funders = sum(n_funders),
  Prop.funders = sum(n_funders) / sum(n),
  N.NIH = sum(n_nih),
  Prop.NIH = sum(n_nih) / sum(n)
) |> 
  t() |>
  kable(digits = 4)
```

## NIH-Funded Datasets

We then look at the number of datasets listed in the DataCite Corpus that list NIH (U.S. National Institutes of Health) as a funder. We check both the funders and fundersROR columns.

```{r nih-data}
#### FUNCTION: nih_subset - argument filename (string) ####
## Argument filename takes the name of a DataCite Corpus file.
## The function returns the subset of observations that list NIH
## as a funder.
get_nih_subset <- function(filename) {
  dat <- read_csv(file = filename, na = c("", "NA", "none")) |>
    filter(
      if_any(any_of(c("funders", "fundersROR")), 
             ~str_detect(., pattern = "(NIH)|(National Institutes of Health)"))
    )
  return(dat)
}

#### FUNCTION: nih_subset - argument filenames (string or vector of strings) ####
## Argument filenames stores names of  DataCite Corpus files. Calls  
## get_nih_subset to return the subset of all DataCite data files, 
## that list NIH as a funder. Returns a dataset.
nih_subset <- function(filenames) {
  cl <- makeCluster(8)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
  
  summ_dc <- foreach(
    fn = filenames,
    .combine = "rbind",
    .export = "get_nih_subset",
    .packages = "tidyverse"
  ) %dopar% {
    get_nih_subset(fn)
  }
  
  stopCluster(cl)
  
  return(summ_dc)
}

# Get subset of DataCite Corpus that are NIH-funded
nih_dat <- nih_subset(files) |> as.data.frame()

# Compute summary statistics across for NIH-funded datasets only
nih_dat |> summarise(
  N.obs = nrow(nih_dat),
  N.doi = sum(!is.na(publication)),
  Prop.doi = sum(!is.na(publication)) / nrow(nih_dat),
  N.cr.date = sum(!is.na(created)),
  Prop.cr.date = sum(!is.na(created)) / nrow(nih_dat),
) |> 
  t() |>
  kable(digits = 4)
```

## Retraction Watch Database

```{r rw-data}
# load retraction watch data
rw <- data.frame(read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashnryn/article-retractions/refs/heads/main/retraction-watch/retraction_watch.csv",
  na.strings = c("", "unavailable")
))

#### Retraction Watch entries without DOIs ####
rw <- rw |> filter(is.na(OriginalPaperDOI))

# What journals are represented?
# rw |> count(Journal) |> arrange(desc(n)) |> head(20)
rw |> filter(str_detect(Journal, pattern = "Conference")) |> nrow() # Majority are conference papers

# Which countries are represented?
rw |> count(Country) |> 
  mutate(p = round(n / nrow(rw), 4)) |> 
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  head(20) # Majority were published in China

rw <- rw |>
  mutate(across(c(OriginalPaperDate, RetractionDate), as.character)) |>
  mutate(pub.year = mdy_hm(OriginalPaperDate) |> year() |> as.integer(), 
         .after = OriginalPaperDate) |>
  mutate(ret.year = mdy_hm(RetractionDate) |> year() |> as.integer(), 
         .after = RetractionDate)

rw$pub.year[which(is.na(rw$pub.year))] = 1753

# Min and max publication dates?
cbind(min.date = min(rw$OriginalPaperDate), 
      max.date = max(rw$OriginalPaperDate))

## The 1953 one is the "first ever english language retraction", per RW
## Benjamin Wilson, "Treatise upon Electricity"

## 2016 is "Expression of FPN and Hepcidin in breast cancer tissues and 
## association of their expression with occurrence of anemia", Shihui Ma, 
## Feihai Ling, et al.

# Retractions without DOIs, by publication year
rw |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pub.year)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "darkgreen") +
    theme_linedraw()

# Restrict to 2000-2026
rw |> filter(!is.na(pub.year)) |>
  filter(pub.year >= 2000 & pub.year <= 2026) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pub.year)) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "darkgreen") +
    theme_linedraw()

# Majority were published in 2010 specifically??
rw |> count(pub.year) |> arrange(desc(n))
```

## DataCite Corpus merged with Retraction Watch

```{r read_rw_mrged}
df <- read_csv("merged.csv")

df |> summarise(
  N.obs = nrow(df),
  N.doi = sum(!is.na(data.citation.id)),
  Prop.doi = sum(!is.na(data.citation.id)) / nrow(df),
  N.cr.date = sum(!is.na(data.created.date)),
  Prop.cr.date = sum(!is.na(data.created.date)) / nrow(df),
  N.data.dois = sum(str_detect(data.id, pattern = "10\\.")),
  Prop.data.dois = sum(str_detect(data.id, pattern = "10\\.")) / nrow(df),
  N.pub.date = sum(!is.na(pub.date)),
  N.funders = sum(!is.na(pub.date)) / nrow(df),
  Prop.funders = sum(!is.na(data.funders)) / nrow(df),
  N.NIH = sum(str_detect(data.funders, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)") |
                str_detect(data.funders.ror, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)"),
              na.rm = TRUE),
  Prop.NIH = sum(str_detect(data.funders, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)") |
                str_detect(data.funders.ror, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)"),
                na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(df)
) |>
  t() |>
  kable(digits = 4)

df |> 
  filter(
      str_detect(data.funders, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)") |
                str_detect(data.funders.ror, pattern = "(NIH)|(NATIONAL INSTITUTES OF HEALTH)")
    ) |>
  select(data.title, data.repository, pub.title, pub.retraction.nature, pub.retraction.reason)
```

There's one retracted paper associated with a data in the DataCite Corpus that also appears in Retraction Watch. Also one of the papers we talked about in the previous article!

### Number of repositories

See which repositories are associated with retracted papers (tables and data visualizations).

```{r repos, fig.height=10}
## For all datasets, with OR without DOIs
# Table
df |> count(data.repository) |> arrange(desc(n))

# Bar graph
df |> 
  filter(!is.na(data.repository) & data.repository != "UNPUBLISHED") |>
  mutate(
      data.repository.mod = str_remove(data.repository, pattern = "\\s\\(.*\\)")
    ) |> 
  mutate(
      data.repository.mod = str_remove(data.repository.mod, pattern = "\\s-\\s.*")
    ) |> 
  count(data.repository.mod) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(data.repository.mod, n), y = n)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "turquoise3") + 
    labs(x = "Repository", y = "Count") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_linedraw()

## For datasets without DOIs
# Table
df |> filter(str_detect(data.id, pattern = "10\\.")) |>
  count(data.repository) |> arrange(desc(n))

# Bar graph
df |> filter(str_detect(data.id, pattern = "10\\.")) |>
  filter(!is.na(data.repository) & data.repository != "UNPUBLISHED") |>
  mutate(
      data.repository.mod = str_remove(data.repository, pattern = "\\s\\(.*\\)")
    ) |> 
  mutate(
      data.repository.mod = str_remove(data.repository.mod, pattern = "\\s-\\s.*")
    ) |> 
  count(data.repository.mod) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(data.repository.mod, n), y = n)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "turquoise3") + 
    labs(x = "Repository", y = "Count") +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_linedraw()
```
